headline: Adaptation is changing to fit circumstances—the core skill for survival in a changing world
universal_truth: The environment changes; those who adapt survive; those who don't, don't
fun_facts: Chameleons change color not just for camouflage but also for temperature regulation and communication
Humans are the most adaptable species on Earth—we live in every climate from arctic to desert
The most adaptable species in history survived all five mass extinctions—cockroaches, sharks, crocodiles
discussion_questions: What have you had to adapt to recently?
How do you balance staying true to yourself and adapting to circumstances?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The dinosaurs were perfect for their world. Then the world changed, and perfection became obsolete. The survivors weren't the strongest or smartest—they were the most adaptable. Adaptation isn't optional; it's the price of continuation.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Adaptation sounds like giving up—changing yourself to fit external demands. But refusing to adapt can mean extinction. What's the balance?
cliff.prompt: When should you adapt versus stand firm?

options.text: Adapt when circumstances genuinely change and old approaches no longer work; stand firm on core values but be flexible on methods
options.response: Yes. Wise adaptation changes methods while preserving purpose. Stubbornness that refuses any change is as dangerous as adaptability that abandons all principles.

options.text: Always stay true to yourself no matter what
options.response: Core values should be stable, but methods and approaches need to evolve...

q1.title: Environment Wins
q1.script: Long-term, the environment always wins. You can resist for a while, but ultimately what doesn't fit, disappears. This isn't fatalism—it's recognizing reality. The question is how to adapt wisely.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Environment Wins"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Core vs Surface
q2.script: Successful adaptation distinguishes core from surface. Change methods, keep purpose. Change tactics, keep strategy. Change expression, keep values. Knowing what to protect and what to change is the art of adaptation.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Proactive Adaptation
q3.script: The best adaptation is proactive—changing before you're forced to. Those who adapt early have options. Those who wait until crisis have only survival mode. Watch for change and adapt ahead of necessity.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The environment changes; those who adapt survive. Be flexible in methods while firm in values. Adapt before you must.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 215. Tomorrow, we'll explore knowledge you're born with—instinct. Until then, identify one adaptation you've been resisting.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Adaptation Inventory - What Needs to Change?
growTrack.activity: What circumstances in your life have changed, but your approach hasn't? Work context, relationship dynamics, personal capabilities? Where are you using old solutions for new problems? Proactive adaptation beats forced crisis response.
